question: What happens when user right-clicks on an empty area of the MS Windows desktop?

options.text: A context menu with view and display settings is opened.

solution:
The Correct answer is __**A context menu with view and display settings is opened.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a user **right-clicks on an empty area** of the MS Windows desktop, a **context menu** appears. This is a feature in the Windows operating system.
 
• The **context menu** provides quick access to various functions and settings related to the desktop, such as **view options, display settings, personalization settings, and screen resolution.**
 
• This feature is designed to enhance **usability and productivity** by offering quick access to frequently-used desktop settings.
 
• The context menu is part of the **graphical user interface (GUI)**, which allows users to interact with the computer using visual elements like icons and menus instead of text-based commands.
 
• Examples of options in the context menu may include **arrange icons, sort by, refresh, new folder creation, and shortcut to display settings.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The File Explorer is launched**__

 __
 
• File Explorer is a **file management tool** in Windows that allows users to navigate, organize, and manage files and folders.
 
• It can be launched by **left-clicking on the File Explorer icon** in the taskbar or by using the **Windows + E** shortcut.
 
• Right-clicking on the desktop does not directly open the File Explorer; this must be done through the Start menu or a shortcut.
 
 
 
• **The Task Manager opens**__
 __
 
• The **Task Manager** is a system monitoring tool in Windows that provides information about running applications, processes, and system performance.
 
• It can be opened by pressing the **Ctrl + Shift + Esc** keys or by right-clicking on the taskbar and selecting "Task Manager."
 
• Right-clicking on the desktop does not open the Task Manager.
 
 
 
• **The Start Menu is displayed**__
 
 
• The **Start Menu** is the central hub for accessing applications, files, and settings in Windows.
 
• It can be accessed by clicking the **Start button** in the bottom-left corner of the screen or by pressing the **Windows key**.
 
• Right-clicking on the desktop does not open the Start Menu.
